statement: In an instance of the stable marriage problem with n men and n women where every participant has a strict, complete preference ordering, the stable matching is unique.
definitions: A matching is stable if there is no blocking pair (m,w) not matched to each other with m preferring w to his partner and w preferring m to hers.
ground_truth_witness: n=3. Men A,B,C with preferences A: Y>X>Z, B: Z>Y>X, C: X>Z>Y. Women X,Y,Z with preferences X: B>A>C, Y: C>B>A, Z: A>C>B. Exactly three of the six perfect matchings are stable: M1={A-Y, B-Z, C-X} (every man gets his 1st choice, every woman her 3rd), M2={A-X, B-Y, C-Z} (everyone gets their 2nd choice), M3={A-Z, B-X, C-Y} (every woman gets her 1st choice, every man his 3rd). None admits a blocking pair, so uniqueness fails.
